name: Operation Ivy
label: Lookout!
lede: A Gilman Street band that lasted two years, played about 185 shows and made one album, Operation Ivy ended up behind Rancid and a good share of third-wave ska.

eras.title: The room that made them
eras.text: Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman had already played together in Basic Radio. With singer Jesse Michaels and drummer Dave Mello they became Operation Ivy in May 1987, and 924 Gilman Street was the room that made them.

yt: Early set at Gilman Street, 1987, from a master VHS
years.h: Operation Ivy plays its first show in Dave Mello's garage
years.p: Wikipedia dates it May 27, 1987, with a first Gilman Street set the next day. The band is Jesse Michaels, Tim Armstrong, Matt Freeman and Mello.
years.xp:
Armstrong and Freeman had played together in the Berkeley ska-punk band Basic Radio. Larry Livermore's account says the two first shared a stage at an Albany High talent show in 1983, and puts the debut in Mello's garage in Albany.

Livermore also says Mello started out on a double-bass-drum kit until Freeman made him drop one and learn a plain four-on-the-floor beat. Of Gilman, Armstrong told him: "The climate was right for Operation Ivy."

years.h: Maximumrocknroll puts "I Got No" and "Officer" on vinyl
years.p: Both songs are on the Gilman Street compilation Turn It Around!, Operation Ivy's first appearance on a record.
years.xp: Rolling Stone says producer Kevin Army recorded the Turn It Around! tracks.

eras.title: Out of Gilman, onto the road
eras.text: Lookout Records put out a six-song 7-inch, and the band became the first Gilman act to tour the country. By mid-1988 Gilman was too small for them.

years.h: A thousand copies of Hectic are gone within a month
years.p: Larry Livermore's Lookout Records presses about 1,000 of the six-song EP, which the band recorded in a single day at Dangerous Rhythm.
years.xp: Livermore says the first pressing sold out inside a month. Wikipedia calls Hectic one of Lookout's best-selling records.

years.cap: Operation Ivy at 924 Gilman Street, from 1988 video footage
yt: Full set at the Boilermaker, St. Louis, 1988
years.h: Six weeks across America in a 1969 Chrysler Newport
years.p: Operation Ivy becomes the first Gilman Street band to tour the country, with Larry Livermore booking the trip.
years.xp:
According to Livermore, they played to three people in El Paso and in Lexington, Kentucky. Freeman remembers the road food: "we ate cheese sandwiches off the hood."

Back in May at Gilman, the crowds were huge and some old scenesters began heckling them as ska boys.

years.h: "Hangin' Out" turns up on Lookout's The Thing That Ate Floyd
years.p: The compilation carries the band's only other 1988 release, next to Bay Area label mates.

eras.title: One album, then they stop
eras.text: They cut one album in days, then chose to stop before a major label could turn them into something else. The last show was in May 1989 at Gilman.

years.cap: Operation Ivy at Barrington Hall, Berkeley, 1989
years.h: Kevin Army gets Energy down in one eight-hour session
years.p: Nineteen songs recorded live at Sound and Vision in San Francisco, one or two takes each.
years.xp:
Army put the band in a semicircle in the tiny room, left the drum room door open for reverb and overdubbed Mello's snares in his bathroom. Paul Bany added saxophone to "Bad Town". Army says he talked the band out of gang shouts on every song by comparing it to the Village People. His philosophy, per Rolling Stone: "Mistakes are okay. Chuck Berry records are filled with them."

Livermore says an earlier try with another engineer went badly, and the band redid it with Army in under a week. Rolling Stone adds that Moon Records had passed on the demos because they did not fit its 2 Tone ska brand.

q: It sort of wasn't that fun anymore.
years.h: Operation Ivy splits with an EMI offer reportedly on the table
years.p: Matt Freeman's reason, as told to Larry Livermore. Wikipedia reports the EMI offer; the band split rather than take the deal.
years.xp:
Freeman said people had started taking the band more seriously than they should have. Armstrong says he and Michaels talked it over at a Telegraph Avenue volleyball court as a mutual decision.

Rolling Stone puts the split before a planned summer 1989 European tour. Wikipedia says the band had played about 185 shows and recorded 32 songs.

yt: The final Gilman show, May 28, 1989, multicam
years.h: Gilman holds more than 1,000 for the last Operation Ivy show
years.p: The room's legal capacity was 300. Green Day played their first show under that name the same night.
years.xp: Livermore also lists the Lookouts and Crimpshrine on the bill. Wikipedia says an unofficial encore followed the next day in a friend's Pinole backyard.

years.h: Energy reaches stores with the band already gone
years.p: Lookout issued the album after the split; sources disagree on the date, March per Wikipedia and two months after the breakup per Rolling Stone.

eras.title: The band that grew after it ended
eras.text: Armstrong and Freeman formed Rancid; Michaels started Big Rig and later Common Rider. Meanwhile the records kept selling and a wave of ska bands cited them.

years.h: Lookout stacks everything on one 27-song CD
years.p: The compilation gathers Energy, Hectic and the Turn It Around! tracks, and becomes how most fans hear the band.

years.h: Reel Big Fish and the Aquabats cover Op Ivy on Take Warning
years.p: Reel Big Fish take "Unity" and Cherry Poppin' Daddies take "Sound System" on the tribute album.

eras.title: The records outlive Lookout
eras.text: Energy passed a gold certification, left Lookout under a royalty dispute, and the members shared a stage once more.

years.h: The RIAA certifies Energy gold, 14 years after the split
years.p: Wikipedia dates it August 8. The band played about 185 shows; the plaque is for the one 19-song album.
Wikipedia says the label removed it from its catalog, as other Lookout bands had also left over money.

years.h: Jesse Michaels sings two Op Ivy songs with Rancid at the Warfield
years.p: Tim Armstrong on a full reunion. At San Francisco's Warfield Theatre, Michaels sang "Unity" and "Sound System", his first stage appearance with them in over 15 years.
years.xp: Michaels has said reunion prospects were poor and that the band never belonged in a big rock club.

years.h: Armstrong's Hellcat reissues the 27-song comp, remastered
years.p: Epitaph's Hellcat imprint puts it out on November 6, then follows in April 2012 with red and clear vinyl of both Energy and Hectic.

years.h: Michaels and Armstrong cut "Living in a Dangerous Land" together
years.p: Their first recording together in 24 years, for Armstrong's Tim Timebomb and Friends series.

years.h: A documentary, Turn It Around, tells the East Bay story
years.p: The film follows the punk scene around Gilman Street, with Operation Ivy in it.

years.cap: Tim Armstrong and Jesse Michaels, c. 2023
years.h: Armstrong and Michaels start DOOM Regulator
years.p: With Circle Jerks drummer Joey Castillo, announced first under the name Bad Optix.

years.h: Laura Jane Grace and Catbite put a live Op Ivy set on record
years.p: Operation Ivy: Live at the Empty Bottle has 27 songs recorded at a Chicago Riot Fest afterparty in September 2024.
